title: ‘Shame and Money’ Director on Sundance-Winning Drama About a Kosovo Family in Free Fall: ‘It’s a Look Into the Past and a Warning to the Future’
full_text: Aug 16, 2026 1:33am PT ‘Shame and Money’ Director on Sundance-Winning Drama About a Kosovo Family in Free Fall: ‘It’s a Look Into the Past and a Warning to the Future’ By Christopher Vourlias Plus Icon Christopher Vourlias Latest ‘Shame and Money’ Director on Sundance-Winning Drama About a Kosovo Family in Free Fall: ‘It’s a Look Into the Past and a Warning to the Future’ 33 minutes ago Sarajevo Industry Head on How Building a Talent Pipeline Makes Markets and Festivals More Vital Than Ever 3 days ago Sarajevo Film Festival Head on How Southeast Europe’s Leading Cinematic Showcase Continues to ‘Forge Its Own Way’ 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Vicky Bane, Schuldenberg Films Sundance Grand Jury Prize winner Visar Morina returns to the Sarajevo Film Festival — the scene of a previous triumph — with the biting social drama “Shame and Money,” which won the top prize in Park City earlier this year and is playing in the festival’s main competition. The director’s third feature wowed audiences at Sundance, where Variety ’s chief film critic Guy Lodge praised the “stoic, slowly lacerating look at economic desperation and exploitation in contemporary Europe” as a “keenly observed, sharp-edged portrait of a Kosovo family divided by class.” Related Stories Mubi to Release ‘La Mesías,’ From ‘La Bola Negra’ Cannes Best Director Winners, in the U.K., Germany, Canada, Australia and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE) Morina’s previous film, “ Exile ,” which also premiered in Park City, won the Sarajevo Film Festival in 2020. That film, about a Kosovan immigrant grappling with paranoia after a string of menacing events, was loosely inspired by the director’s own experience. Born in Kosovo, Morina emigrated with his family to Germany in the 1990s, before the war that would ultimately lead to the country’s independence. Popular on Variety “Shame and Money” follows Shaban (Astrit Kabashi) and Hatixhe (Flonja Kodheli), a couple in their forties living with their extended family in rural Kosovo, where they eke out a modest living on their farm. When a family dispute leads to a terrible act of betrayal, their livelihood is suddenly lost. Along with Shaban’s mother and the couple’s young daughters, they are forced to move to Pristina, where the pressure to provide weighs heavily on both husband and wife. Piecing together odd jobs, they do their best to find a way in the hyper-capitalist Kosovan capital, until the relentless struggle of daily life pushes Shaban to the breaking point. Though deeply rooted in the sociopolitical realities of Kosovo, a country that’s largely failed to make good on the promises of the post-war order, Morina sees “Shame and Money” as a parable of modern-day Europe. Across the continent, he notes, the rising cost of living, housing shortages, stagnant wages and a growing rift between the haves and have-nots has spurred widespread pessimism about the direction in which society seems to be heading. “We are actually coming to a point in Germany where it feels like we are going straight to a situation like this in Kosovo,” Morina says. “It’s a look into the past and a warning to the future.” The film provides a bleak portrait of Kosovo, a war-scarred country whose social fabric is fraying at the seams: a society where, as Shaban is reminded by his brother-in-law, Alban (Alban Ukaj), a nouveau riche businessman who reluctantly agrees to take in the struggling family, “Everything has its place. And every person, too.” For the husband and wife duo, that means a succession of low-skilled, low-wage jobs as they scrap to make ends meet. The rigid taxonomy of contemporary urban life couldn’t be more apparent: When Shaban is offered a job as a night watchman at a gated community rising on the city’s outskirts, he explains to Hatixhe that it is a job “to keep out poor people like us.” Gradually, Shaban becomes a ghost of himself, in what comes to feel like a natural outcome in a society where a man’s value can be calculated down to the very last cent. “‘When you’re broke, even your mom doesn’t love you,’” Morina recalls a Kosovan man once telling him. “There is nothing I associate more strongly with the film than this phrase.” “Shame and Money” is written by Morina and Doruntina Basha. It’s produced by Vicky Bane and Schuldenberg Films in co-production with Eagle Eye Films, Vertigo Ljubljana, On Film Production, List Production and Quetzalcoatl. World sales are being handled by The Yellow Affair and Espoo. In both of his most recent features, Morina has been preoccupied with the lives of outsiders — those who, either because of immigration (“Exile”) or class status (“Shame and Money”), are shunted to the periphery of society. Increasingly, it seems those dividing lines have become chasms. At a time when the world (briefly) christened its first trillionaire and the ruling classes build underground bunkers or dream of blasting off into outer space, “Shame and Money” provides a stark warning about the direction in which things are trending — both for our societies and ourselves. “I really believe that people can only take shit to a certain extent. At some point, they go crazy,” says Morina. “There is this German word sozialer Frieden — social harmony. And I think at some point, there is a point of no return.” The Sarajevo Film Festival runs Aug. 14 – 21. This AI Startup Made a 24-Hour AI News Channel. Who Wants This? Loading comments... title: ‘Too Much Music’ Is a Doc Project About Ghanaian Keyboardist Kiki Gyan – and About Who Controls Artists’ Narratives
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 15, 2026 11:59pm 'Too Much Music' Courtesy of Locarno Open Doors Music is a blessing, but maybe it can also be a curse – especially if you are a famous musician who gets remembered mostly for drugs and other negative narratives. Too Much Music , one of the works-in-progress showcased at the 2026 edition of Open Doors , the Locarno Film Festival ‘s co-production platform and talent development program for filmmakers from equity-seeking communities and regions where artistic expression is at risk, wants to explore all these issues. It comes from director Aseye Fiagbe (short The Gentleman , episode 7 of Bad Mama ) and puts a spotlight on a famous keyboardist from Ghana, Kiki Gyan. Related Stories Movies 'Mission' Stars George MacKay and Rosy McEwen on Capitalism, Creative Freedom and the Eternal Allure of British Independent Film Movies Locarno Film Festival Awards Go to 'You Don't Belong Here,' Hong Sangsoo, Monica Bellucci The director is also the producer of the doc via her Aseye Fiagbe Creative Studio in Ghana. She presented the project during the second edition of Open Doors with a focus on films from Africa and won one of three Open Doors Grants . THR has compiled highlights about the movie and insight from Fiagbe about the project and the themes it explores. Synopsis Too Much Music is a feature documentary about Kiki Gyan, a Ghanaian keyboard prodigy who rose to international fame as a teenager with Afro-rock pioneers Osibisa. As his musical contributions expanded without recognition, tensions around credit and ownership led him to leave the band and pursue a solo career across London, Lagos and New York, shaping African disco and funk in the process. Over time, the same system that profited from his brilliance proved indifferent to his vulnerability, and his life became reduced to a singular narrative of addiction and demise. Through archival material and testimonies from family and collaborators, the film reconstructs the forces that shaped his journey and asks how artists are remembered, who controls their stories, and what is lost when brilliance is reframed as failure. Director’s note Music is a blessing, and Kiki Gyan had that gift in abundance. His music is joyful, infectious, technically brilliant, and yet his life story often overshadows the work itself. Many people know how he died long before they encounter the music he made. That imbalance is what pulled me into this film. I grew up with Osibisa as the soundtrack of Sunday afternoons in my home. Years later, I discovered Kiki’s solo work and realized how much of his brilliance had been hidden behind a simplified story of addiction and death. Too Much Music is not about rescuing him or forcing his life into a neat redemption arc. I am interested in complexity: holding brilliance, failure, joy, exploitation, vulnerability, and legacy in the same frame. As a Ghanaian filmmaker, I see this film as part of a larger responsibility to document our cultural history with care. Kiki’s story is about memory and erasure, about who gets remembered for their work and who is remembered only for how they fell. What was the inspiration for you to want to make this film? I grew up with Osibisa as part of the soundtrack of life in Ghana, but the story I knew about Kiki Gyan was basically the story of how he died. He was a brilliant prodigy who became addicted to drugs, lost everything and died in a church bathroom. That was the story. Then, as an adult, I started discovering how much music he had actually made and how little of it I knew. I realized that, like many other Ghanaians, I knew the ending of his life before I really knew the work. That bothered me, and the more I researched him, the more complicated, colorful and human the story became. How universal are the themes of the film, and why should people outside Mozambique see it? For me, the film is ultimately about memory and who gets reduced to what. We do this all the time. A whole person can become one mistake, one tragedy, one headline. Kiki’s story happens within a very particular Ghanaian and African music history, but the questions underneath it feel universal. What happens when talent arrives before someone is ready for everything that comes with it? Who gets credit for creative work? How do we treat people when they fall from the pedestal we put them on? And who gets to decide what remains of someone after they are gone? I don’t think you need to know Kiki Gyan or Osibisa to recognize those questions. What is the next step for you and your collaborators after Open Doors? Open Doors gave the project a real push forward, through the conversations we had, the connections forged and the award, which gives us so much room to continue the development work. The writing and research are still ongoing, particularly around London, Lagos and the U.S., and we are continuing our archival research while building the international production structure around the film. A big focus now is following up with the producers, financiers and other partners I met in Locarno and finding the right co-production relationships. We came to Locarno with a Ghanaian film looking for the right international collaborators. I left feeling much clearer about what those relationships should actually look like. THR

title: Ranveer Singh, Kalyani Priyadarshan’s ‘Pralay,’ Produced by Ananya Birla and Hansal Mehta, Directed by Jai Mehta, Starts Filming
full_text: Aug 15, 2026 10:41pm PT Ranveer Singh, Kalyani Priyadarshan’s ‘Pralay,’ Produced by Ananya Birla and Hansal Mehta, Directed by Jai Mehta, Starts Filming By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Ranveer Singh, Kalyani Priyadarshan’s ‘Pralay,’ Produced by Ananya Birla and Hansal Mehta, Directed by Jai Mehta, Starts Filming 3 hours ago Zee Entertainment Wins Interim Relief to Proceed With $330 Million Capital Raise Despite Indian Regulator’s Market Ban 1 day ago ‘The Greatest Showman’ Stage Musical Sets Spring 2027 Opening at London’s Theatre Royal Drury Lane 1 day ago See All Birla Studios/True Story Films/Maa Kasam Films Ranveer Singh ‘s “ Pralay ,” an end-of-the-world action thriller, has begun filming in Mumbai. The film is produced by Ananya Birla’s Birla Studios , Hansal Mehta and Sahil Saigal’s True Story Films and Singh’s Maa Kasam Films. Singh, who headlines the project, also serves as a producer on the film, which is directed by Jai Mehta. One of the top stars of Bollywood, Singh takes on a physically demanding role for “Pralay.” This is his next project after the “Dhurandhar” (2025) and “Dhurandhar – The Revenge” (2026) duology, which are among the highest-grossing Indian films of all time. Popular on Variety Related Stories Mubi to Release ‘La Mesías,’ From ‘La Bola Negra’ Cannes Best Director Winners, in the U.K., Germany, Canada, Australia and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE) The cast also includes Kalyani Priyadarshan, who broke out with “Lokah Chapter One: Chandra” (2025), in a pivotal role. Jai Mehta previously co-directed SonyLIV series “Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story” (2020) with Hansal Mehta , and directed JioHotstar series “Lootere” (2024). “Pralay” is an original story centered on survival as the world faces catastrophe, set against the backdrop of Mumbai, where the production is now shooting. The production is filming at live locations across the Mumbai region, an approach the makers say brings added scale, texture and realism to the story. The crew includes talent from India and abroad. Birla Studios said the project reflects Birla’s interest in working with some of the leading current names in Indian cinema. True Story Films, run by Hansal Mehta and Sahil Saigal, said the film fits the banner’s focus on unconventional storytelling. “It’s the kind of film that India hasn’t made yet, the kind of film that India hasn’t seen before,” Hansal Mehta had told Variety while unveiling the True Story Films slate. “Pralay” moved into production after several months of technically intensive pre-production. title: Disney Unveils Avengers Infinity Defense Lead By Ms. Marvel, Return Of Avengers Cast, Harrison Ford Models New Indiana Jones Attraction, Villains Land & More At D23
full_text: Skip to main content By Destiny Jackson Destiny Jackson Crafts Editor, Awards @DestinyDreadful More Stories By Destiny Disney Unveils Avengers Infinity Defense Lead By Ms. Marvel, Return Of Avengers Cast, Harrison Ford Models New Indiana Jones Attraction, Villains Land & More At D23 All Things Spidey At D23: Tom Holland, Anniversary Comic Book, ‘Friendly Neighborhood’ Sneak-Peak, ‘Amazing Friends’ Renewal & Upcoming Special ‘Spidey and the Avengers: Halloween Team-Up!’ Lucasfilm Co-Boss Dave Filoni On ‘Hunt For Ben Solo’ Pic Future: “The Force Is Not With Us…” – D23 View All August 15, 2026 10:21pm Disney California Adventure Park Avengers Campus Disney/Marvel The happiest place on earth just got more global. At the D23 ’s Saturday Parks Panel, host Neil Patrick Harris gave way to several Walt Disney Imagineers who shared the next steps in the mouse house’s billion-dollar expansion . ​ In the U.S., executives and creative designers showed off a sneak peek of upcoming West Coast attractions at Disney California Adventure. Coming to Avengers Campus to join the likes of Guardians of the Galaxy – Mission: Breakout! and Web Slingers: A Spider-Man Adventure are two new attractions. The first is a flight-spinning ride called Stark Flight Lab, which will see guests take on training trips from returning Avengers cast members Robert Downey Jr., Anthony Mackie and Brie Larson. The second big-ticket attraction will be Avengers Infinity Defense, a ride that puts the fight against Thanos in the hands of park visitors. As they enter, riders will receive special mission orders from Ms. Marvel (featuring a role reprisal from Iman Vellani) and team up with Avengers and their returning actors, Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), Captain America (Mackie), Thor (Chris Hemsworth) and Iron Man (Downey Jr.). Both attractions will open in 2028. Joining ranks with Walt Disney World, DCA will also become home to the Na’vi via an Avatar Destination to be announced at a later date. Watch on Deadline ¡Mira! A new look at the Coco-themed attraction coming to Disney California Adventure 🎶✨ #D23 #Disneyland pic.twitter.com/y3qTEjVlKi — Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026 Over on the East Coast, the Walt Disney World resort is breaking ground on its latest attraction, Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent, which becomes the first park to involve titular star Harrison Ford as an animatronic model. Ford, who could not attend in person, sent a video explaining his excitement at being involved in the ride mechanics for the first time. While Tokyo Disney, Disneyland Paris and Disneyland have established Indiana Jones attractions, this will be Walt Disney World’s first. We have unearthed Indiana Jones news 🤠 For the first time ever, Harrison Ford is the actual model of the Indiana Jones Audio-Animatronics figure, fear of snakes included 🌳 #D23 #AnimalKingdom #WaltDisneyWorld pic.twitter.com/NULBc78sUe — Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026 Director and head of Walt Disney Animation Jared Bush came out to talk about an Encanto ride called Antonio’s Fiesta de Encanto; all of the cast from the film will be reprising their roles. Housed in the film’s iconic Casita, guests are invited to Antonio’s Gifts Day, where he receives the power to communicate with animals. Riders will travel through the Madrigal family’s home on pieces of elaborate, colorful furniture, viewing the story of the house while interacting with more than 50 animals throughout the attraction. Attractions for Encanto – coming to Animal Kingdom – and Villains – coming to Magic Kingdom | #D23 pic.twitter.com/Vdf8RfsoKW — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 14, 2026 ​ And finally, though Disney remains the number one home for “happily ever afters,” Imagineering has been brewing up a wicked side. Villains Land, which is exactly what it sounds like, is the destination for fans of all baddies. Executives teased that the Walt Disney World attraction will contain a high-thriller roller coaster experience on Maleficent’s thorny briar mountain top featuring “elements never attempted before on a Disney theme park attraction,” and another flume ride will feature the Evil Queen’s Magic Mirror, who might get to tell his side of the Snow White story. title: Disney’s Experiences Chief Talks Figment, the Tomorrowland Refresh and All That D23 News
full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All August 15, 2026 9:57pm Villains Land concept art Disney Experiences Saturday evening in Anaheim’s Honda Center, The Walt Disney Co. turned to Neil Patrick Harris to serve as a master of ceremonies for what is surely one of its most scrutinized events: The Disney Experiences showcase presentation at D23 . D23 of course is Disney’s in-house fan convention, and the showcase panels are used to reveal new projects and make news. Disney turned to a late night theme for the event, with Harris hosting, joined by a live band, opening the event with a monologue full of Disney-related quips, like noting that the last host of the Experiences was Josh D’Amaro. Related Stories Business Disney and Epic Games Launch Game That Connects Star Wars Theme Park Ride to New Fortnite Adventure Movies 'Frozen 3' "Royal Wedding" Between Anna and Kristoff Is Crashed by New Villain in First-Look “Wait a minute. If my math is correct, I am 24 months away from being CEO, and 48 months away from owning the Lakers,” Harris quipped, before launching into an animatronic-themed, cameo-filled musical number. Of course, it is D23, so it was the announcements that the fans wer eager to see. Saturday’s showcase ended with a pair of showstoppers for Disney theme park fans, a refresh of Figment, one of Epcot’s original rides, including the return of the Dreamfinder character, and a revitalization of Disneyland ‘s Tomorrowland, one of Walt Disney’s original visions. The concept: “New attractions, new open spaces, new places to dream about the future.” “This particular Tomorrowland here at Disneyland was the one that was originally thought of and designed by Walt himself,” says Thomas Mazloum, the chairman of Disney Experiences, in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter . “If you think about it, so much of that at the time was based on optimism: Optimism about the future, and this is going to be our North Star as we approach this particular work. It doesn’t mean we’re not going to change things. It just means we respect where we came from, but we use that optimism to carry us in the future, and in the case of this particular project, I think it proves we are listening carefully to what our guests are telling us while investing also in new generations. “We’ve done a lot, as you know, on Disney California Adventure, and we’re going to continue to do more. But we also know we need to listen equally as carefully and harmonize what this icon, especially Disneyland, did to the world when it first opened,” Mazloum continued. “And so the way I approach this is really not to be beholden by the past, to respect it, but to take Walt’s original positiveness, this optimism, and use that as our inspiration for the creative that we’re going to introduce.” Of course that wasn’t the only news Disney had to share. There were updates on new lands and projects announced two years ago like the Cars -themed area and Villains Land at Magic Kingdom, cruise ship updates, and plenty more. Mazloum spoke to THR ahead of the event to lay the groundwork for what the company is teeing up over the coming months and years, and his first few months leading the division succeeding D’Amaro, who is now Disney’s CEO. “It’s been very simple and very smooth, Alex. Truth be told, even in my prior roles, I’ve reported to Josh D’Amaro, and in this role I continue to report to him. I’m very familiar with our businesses, and it was very exciting for me, frankly speaking, to travel,” Mazloum says, noting that he went to every Disney resort around the world, and many of its cruise ships, after taking the top job. “Recently, I shared a note with our team around the world, and I said to them in my final sentence, and I meant this: ‘This is the privilege of my lifetime.’ “The reason why I feel that way is traveling around the world made me once again realize we truly are having more projects currently happening than at any single point in our history, and it isn’t just the volume — and we’re going to share this obviously with our fans this week — it’s the creativity. And what I always think about is our founder Walt’s quote when he said, ‘Disneyland will never be completed if there is enough imagination left in the world,’ and imagine me traveling all around the world, looking at each side, seeing everything starting to come to life.” While D23 in 2024 served as an unveiling for a barrage of projects that will bring new Disney IP to its theme parks and resorts around the world, this year’s event put more focus on the parks’ own IP. That includes Tomorrowland, of course, but also fan favorites like Figment, the dragon at who has become something of a mascot for Epcot in Orlando, and the yeti animatronic on the Expedition Everest ride at Animal Kingdom, which has been broken since shortly after the ride opened. “What that really means to me is that we’re listening to all of our fans and our guests, and specifically that means harmonizing the various demands,” Mazloum says. “You might be familiar with what we do here at Disneyland, with Avengers Campus, Coco , the first-time attractions and IPs that not only satisfy our existing audience, but I believe will also appeal to new audiences, while harmonizing the need to pay attention also to what our existing fans that have been loyal for many years and often decades demand of us, and to do that is to make sure that we revitalize fan favorites and keep them nice and fresh and new, while also working on new lands, and it’s about really harmonizing these tools. “What you will see is all the new lands and updates on everything that we have announced, and how we follow through, and how we put the creativity at work to create a world-class experience, but then you will also see as we talk about Figment, as we talk about Yeti, as we talk about Tomorrowland, you will see the focus on the existing guests that have been longing for this for a long time,” he added. Things like the yeti animatronic might seem like small potatoes in the grand scheme of things, but Mazloum frames them as a core piece of the Disney magic, getting families to return again and again, generation after generation. “We are immensely focused on attention to details, and our guests, our fans, they genuinely care about our places, our parks, our cruise ships. They genuinely care about the stories,” he says. “They understand our commitment to tell our stories in an authentic way, the way only Disney can, and they hold us to a high standard. And our goal is to meet and exceed that standard. “Whether it’s a nostalgic ride, whether it’s something like the Yeti, it may just be one small thing, but this is really something — a relationship between us and our fans that that we treasure and that is paying off,” he adds. Disney’s Carousel of Progress at Disney World, for example, will be updated next year not only with new scenes, but also new voices, with Jamie Lee Curtis and Bryan Cranston set to voice characters on the attraction. There will also be updates on the Disney Cruise Line, which has become a major source of investment for the company, with a flurry of new ships set to be delivered over the next half decade, including a new lightly smaller class of ships that Mazloum says will enable the company to add new locations in Alaska and Europe to its itineraries. “It gives us a ton of flexibility, which we really want and need as we expand the cruise line both domestically and globally,” Mazloum says. “I always tell everyone it’s three vacations in one. You get the convenience of a cruise, especially for multi-generational travel, you get the Disney stories, and then you get your beach vacation or the beautiful destinations. “So it’s a really incredible value proposition, and with our growing portfolio of parks around the globe — in future years, as you know, we also are working on another park in Abu Dhabi — but when you think about our global portfolio of parks right now, what the ships enable us is to a reach more people in the world that are Disney fans, and at the same time also connect them to our parks,” he adds. “Then you couple that with the fact that there’s still a sizable amount of the population that have never cruised, and on Disney Cruise Line in particular, we attract one of the highest amount of new to cruise guests in the industry.” The next Wish-class ship, the Disney Believe, will include a statue of Moana in its atrium. Ultimately Mazloum is betting that D23 will underscore how the company is leaning into what its theme park fans want, and can set the stage for his own tenure atop the most important experiential entertainment business in the world. “What I’m really hoping that the fans will see, especially at this D23, is the creativity that we’re applying to all the new experiences we’ve announced, and how much we are listening to them, and how important their thoughts and their feelings are to us in in us reimagining some of their most favorite attractions, characters, or lands,” he says. “We’re gonna prove to the world and to our fans that we are following through on all the announcements we made two years ago. That we haven’t just announced it, we’re actually following through.” THR

title: ‘Monsters, Inc.’ Themed Land Will Open at Disney World in 2027
full_text: Aug 15, 2026 9:11pm PT ‘Monsters, Inc.’ Themed Land Will Open at Disney World in 2027 By Jazz Tangcay Plus Icon Jazz Tangcay Artisans Editor @jazzt Latest ‘Monsters, Inc.’ Themed Land Will Open at Disney World in 2027 5 hours ago ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race,’ ‘All Stars’ and ‘Untucked’ Renewed for New Seasons at MTV and Paramount+ 9 hours ago ‘Lilo & Stitch 2’ Drops First Look of Pink Alien Angel in Live-Action Sequel 1 day ago See All Disney THe’Monsters, Inc.’ themed land, Monstropolis is set to open at Disney’s Hollywood Studios at Disney World in 2027. The news was announced Saturday at D23 . Vice President Creative, Walt Disney World Portfolio at Walt Disney Imagineering, Michael Hundgen told Variety , “We’re so excited to bring Monstropolis to life for fans.” Currently under construction, Monstropolis will transport visitors into the world of Sulley and Mike. Related Stories Mubi to Release ‘La Mesías,’ From ‘La Bola Negra’ Cannes Best Director Winners, in the U.K., Germany, Canada, Australia and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE) According to Disney, guests will have the chance to explore the city, meet its citizens, taste unique cuisine, and step into the everyday world of monsters in a totally new way. For the first time, two worlds—once separated—are coming face to face, not through screams, but through laughter. Popular on Variety Hundgen explained, “’Monsters, Inc’ is right up there in terms of iconic locations. The moment you saw it, you thought, ‘I want to go to a world where monsters live and work and play.’ And so, to get to do that at the scale that we’re doing it at is phenomenal. Not only is it about the breadth of the land, but also about creating some of these iconic locations that we’ve seen in the films throughout the years that we’re now getting to realize.’” A central element of Monstropolis is its theatrical experience, which Hundgen emphasized as an important addition to the land. “We knew the door coaster was the cornerstone of the experience,” he said. “It feels like just giving them a coaster would shortchange the experience. So, we embarked on this idea of a theater experience that would really orient our guests to Monsters. We’re inviting folks into this land for the first time, and the monsters are a little skittish around that, so they’re kind of feeling us out. For so long they’ve been sometimes as afraid of us as we are of them, and so this idea that we’re all working in harmony together is new to them.” Hundgen explained that it wouldn’t be a typical theater experience. Collaborating with Pixar and Industrial Light & Magic, the team has developed high-definition panels combined with physical characters. In addition to humor and heart, the show will feature a new original song written exclusively for the park by composer Randy Newman.“It’s the first time Randy has ever written something exclusively for a Disney theme park,” Hundgen revealed, calling the song a perfect complement to the high-thrill rollercoaster that will be located nearby. Disney’s first-ever suspended rollercoaster ride will be a major highlight of the land. “It’s a showstopper,” Hundgen declared. “It’s the first hanging coaster we’ve ever done at Disney anywhere in the world. That opening scene will take you straight into the laugh floor, and guests will be placed into contraptions that Mike has created to harness both laughs and screams. The idea is that if you combine those two things—well, screams are powerful, but laughs are even more powerful.” The ride will take guests 40 feet high in four seconds, he teases. “When you think about show-stopping moments in our canon, that is going to be up there as one of the biggest and best that we’ve ever seen.” The rollercoaster will take guests 40 feet high in just four seconds. “When you think about show-stopping moments in our canon, this will rank as one of the biggest and best,” Hundgen teased. He credited the Imagineering team and their research and development efforts for pushing the boundaries of innovation. “Some of the techniques we’re using in the theater itself come from our partnerships with R&D and ILM,” he said. “More importantly, it’s about using technology to support the story we’re telling. What can we do to deepen the emotional connection guests have with these characters while using tech to enable that?” Hundgen also noted the use of innovative techniques in both the theater and coaster experience. “We’re drawing inspiration from immersive theater and optical illusions that make you feel like things are actually there—paired with physical elements that truly are there,” he explained. “You’ll see plenty of that in the theater experience, as well as a few tricks in the coaster that combine old-school illusions with new tech, all infused with the humor and heart of these characters.” In addition to the theatrical experience and the rollercoaster, Monstropolis will feature merchandise locations and new restaurants—Disney staples. Among them will be Archie’s Scare Pig Pizza, inspired by the mascot from “Monsters University,” and Harryhausen’s, the sushi restaurant featured in the first film where Mike and Celia went on their date. “We’re reimagining Harryhausen’s as a brand-new space,” Hundgen shared. “The menu will be wildly fun. Imagine sushi dishes inspired by the monster world: sushi rolls, tempura satays, all with iconic names that feel straight out of the film.” Guests can also look forward to an animatronic octopus sushi chef. “We’re going to have a full-on animatronic sushi octopus figure, cooking up sushi and playing host,” he confirmed. Monstropolis is scheduled to open in 2027, with restaurants, merchandise experiences, and the theater show debuting alongside the new land. Hundgen expressed excitement about the ambitious project. “Monsters, being one of the first out the gate, will really raise the bar. It’s an incredible project team—passionate and dedicated—and they’ve worked through some pretty gnarly challenges. This will be a fantastic addition to Hollywood Studios and Walt Disney World as a whole. It’s going to be quite the destination.” This AI Startup Made a 24-Hour AI News Channel. Who Wants This? title: Netflix Fires Back Against Tyra Banks’ ‘America’s Next Top Model’ Docuseries Defamation Lawsuit
full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 15, 2026 8:03pm Tyra Banks in 'Reality Check: Inside America's Next Top Model.' Netflix has filed a motion to strike and dismiss Tyra Banks ‘ defamation lawsuit against Netflix over her portrayal in the streamer’s America’s Next Top Model docuseries, entitled Reality Check . Banks filed a lawsuit against Netflix in June, where she argued she was falsely represented in the docuseries, arguing that her comments were “stripped of context and reassembled to support a false and defamatory narrative unrelated to what she actually expressed.” She participated in a three-and-a-half hour long interview, outlining that just 16 minutes of her footage was used for Reality Check . Related Stories TV Netflix Picks Up YA Series 'Sunshine Girls,' Adds Randall Park to 'Minimum Wage' TV Supernatural YA Romance 'Sid & Zoey' Nabs Netflix Pickup Netflix’s motion, which was filed Friday, argues that Banks’ complaints are “about ordinary editorial decisions.” The motion confirms that Banks sat for a three-and-a-half-hour interview, adding that “After the interview, [Banks] signed an agreement granting the filmmakers the right to edit her interview footage, acknowledging she had ‘no right to review or approve’ the finished documentary, and releasing claims arising from it — including for defamation and false light. She now alleges the documentary, Reality Check: Inside America’s Next Top Model (the ‘Documentary’), defames her — not because it says anything false about her, but because she wanted advance notice of what another interviewee would say, more of her interview included, and her perspective presented differently.” In Banks’ lawsuit, she specifically cited how she was shown in the docuseries responding to cycle two contestant Shandi Sullivan’s alleged sexual assault during filming. She was shown being asked “You remember the story with Shandi?” in Reality Check , to which she responded “um,” before the screen cuts to black, creating a “devastating and deliberate” implication that Banks couldn’t remember the assault, she argued in her suit. “And when Banks is asked whether she remembers Sullivan’s story, the Documentary shows her answer: ‘I do remember her story.’ A documentary expressly showing Banks remembering does not imply that she forgot,” Netflix’s motion reads in response. “Banks understands editorial discretion. She created, hosted, and executive produced 24 seasons of ANTM , making the same kinds of editorial decisions she now attacks — what footage to include, what to omit, and how to present competing narratives,” the motion continues. “The Documentary simply turned that editorial lens back on ANTM and Banks. Her disagreement with the resulting portrayal does not make it defamatory.” A Netflix spokesperson told ABC News in a statement Friday they plan to “vigorously defend” the docuseries and those behind it. “Directors Daniel Sivan and Mor Loushy are respected documentarians who thoroughly interviewed the people behind America’s Next Top Model ,” the statement reads. “Tyra Banks was given the opportunity to speak openly about her experience and the creators fairly presented her perspective alongside those of every other participant shown in this documentary. We stand behind Reality Check: Inside America’s Next Top Model and will continue to vigorously defend it.” The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to Banks’ lawyer for comment. THR

title: Disney D23 Takeaway: With ‘X-Men’, ‘Tangled’, ‘Incredibles 3’ & More, Movie Studio Poised To Slay In 2028
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Disney D23 Takeaway: With ‘X-Men’, ‘Tangled’, ‘Incredibles 3’ & More, Movie Studio Poised To Slay In 2028 Lucasfilm Co-Boss Dave Filoni On ‘Hunt For Ben Solo’ Pic Future: “The Force Is Not With Us…” – D23 ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Super $67M Third Weekend; ‘Odyssey’ Sailing Past Half Billion, Dinos Fight For Third – Box Office Update View All August 15, 2026 6:18pm Disney teases upcoming slate at 2026 D23. Disney/Pixar/Marvel Studios The morning after an intoxicating D23 Friday night, which included a dancing spirit squad, Adam Driver and Inde Navarrette X-Men surprises, Josh Gad crooning, Ryan Gosling, Anne Hathaway and confetti raining, it became really clear — Disney is going to have a killer 2028 at the box office. And they haven’t even filled out the entire year’s slate yet. With the 2026 domestic box office racking toward an estimated $10 billion stateside, will people still be going to the cinemas two years from now? Hell yes, if Disney has anything to do with it. Related Stories Books All Things Spidey At D23: Tom Holland, Anniversary Comic Book, 'Friendly Neighborhood' Sneak-Peak, 'Amazing Friends' Renewal & Upcoming Special 'Spidey and the Avengers: Halloween Team-Up!' News Lucasfilm Co-Boss Dave Filoni On 'Hunt For Ben Solo' Pic Future: "The Force Is Not With Us..." - D23 Disney has 14 dates currently in the Rentrak system for 2028 — and that’s not counting 20th Century Studios or Searchlight theatrical releases. Again, dates can always shed, but with the few tentpole dates that were announced last night at D23’s The Ultimate Disney Fan Event at the Anaheim Honda Center, coupled with what we already know, it would not be shocking if 2028 has a shot at rivaling Disney’s record global year at the B.O., which was 2019 with $13.15B (that’s when they were fully merged with 20th Century Fox). Watch on Deadline Right now for 2028, if the studio can keep these productions on track, Disney has dated: Pixar original Ghost Market – March 10 Currently, no other wide release is dated against it. Live-action Tangled – March 31 Amazon MGM Studios has a Chosen movie already on the schedule which is counter-programming to this highly anticipated feature adaptation of the 2010 animated pic. Tangled arrives in theaters a week ahead of Sony’s The Beatles – Four Films The Beginning on April 7, 2028. Marvel’s untiled X-Men – May 5 The MCU returns to its formerly prized summer launchpad, three years after 2025’s Thunderbolts* . Who dare date against this revival? In the hands of Feige, it’s not like Bryan Singer’s old stuff. From the looks of last night, per Hugh Jackman’s beam-in, he ain’t coming back as Wolverine. Live-action Lilo & Stitch 2 – Memorial Day weekend, May 28 Currently, Lionsgate has Resurrection of the Christ: Part Two on this date. Again, counter-programming skewing to an older adult religious demo. The two can co-exist, but depending on how successful Part One is (May 6, 2027), it would’t be shocking if Lionsgate changes their mind in the face of a five-quad sequel to a billion-dollar movie. Pixar’s Incredibles 3 – June 16 Before D23, Disney already announced the Fathers Day weekend date for the threequel to one of the highest grossing animated movies of all-time ( Incredibles 2 at $1.2B). The kids—Violet, Dash and Jack Jack—are the same height, but grown up in their superhero abilities as the conceit here is that they sneak out of the house more. No other major studio pics are versing Incredibles 3 yet. Marvel’s Ghost Rider – announced for 2028 without a specific date on the Gosling starring, Shawn Levy directed feature, but a good guess is that it’s going to July 28 that year as Disney has that weekend on hold in Rentrak. If it is July 28, well, that’s the penultimate end of summer date where Deadpool & Wolverine , Brand New Day and Fantastic Four: First Steps have soared. You’d be crazy to date against this movie. Marvel’s Black Panther 3 – Dec. 15, 2028 Clearly, the Christmas event movie of the year. Universal has an untitled tentpole dated five days later on Dec. 20. That’s quite a killer lineup on paper alone, and more powerful from what’s already on deck in 2027 for Disney, which we’ll sift through below. Here’s some takeaways from last night’s fireworks: (L-R) Maya Boyd, Inde Navarrette, Samara Weaving, Christopher Abbott, Kit Connor, Jake Schreier, and Sadie Sink speak onstage at the Disney Entertainment Showcase at D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event on August 14, 2026 in Anaheim, California. (Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney) Marvel Cinematic Universe Movies Are No Longer in Superhero Fatigue With three MCU titles dated for 2028, that’s absolutely clear, and with MCU Boss Kevin Feige involved in the success of Sony’s highest grossing movie of all-time, the Marvel Studios co-production Spider-Man: Brand New Day at $1.8B+, “It’s not about IP,” says one Disney executive talking about the success of that rival film. “It’s about making great movies. Spider-Man: Brand New Day isn’t successful because it’s a Spider-Man movie, it’s successful because it’s an excellent, fun movie.” That’s the plan for MCU going forward: Reliable and fun-filled filmmakers and talent like Ryan Gosling and Shawn Levy involved in Ghost Rider , and a murderers’ row of thespians in X-Men such as Driver, Obsession breakout Navarrette, Christopher Abbott and Samara Weaving, to name a few. There was some cynicism from fans over the Avengers: Doomsday trailer that was released around San Diego Comic-Con, which is to be expected. You can’t spoil everything in a trailer for a highly anticipated sequel. Also, who isn’t going to watch this upside-down universe MCU movie where Iron Man ‘s Robert Downey Jr. is Victor Werner von Doom? The clip released last night shows this is a more complex, sinister strategist than Josh Brolin’s crash-bang-boom baddie Thanos from the previous Avengers pics. Screams Pedro Pascal’s Reed Richards, “Answer me, Victor! Why did you do this?” Masses will want to know well into early 2027 in what’s an optimistic start to Disney’s 2027 box office year. Joker: Folie a Deux , this is not. And after the better-than-Barbenheimer success of The Odyssey and Brand New Day in the marketplace, it’s clear we won’t have a problem of two male fandom-charged properties like Doomsday and Dune: Part 3 getting in each other’s way. Both battalion boats will rise at the B.O. Kathryn Hahn and Mother Gothel from ‘Tangled’ Kathryn Wirsing/Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures Live Action Takes Of Disney Classics Aren’t Going Away While Honda Center denizens last night could only get excited by less than a minute’s tease of Tangled , which showed Rapunzel’s long blonde hair and Kathryn Hahn briefly as notorious Mother Gothel, Disney isn’t bailing on bringing legacy animated classics into the flesh with even Moana recently falling off her surfboard with less than $300M at the global box office. Disney’s plan per sources going forward remains, of course, spacing out animated sequels from their live-action counterparts, as well as finding a unique way into beloved vault titles (i.e. a Bridesmaids -like spinoff of Cinderella from Akiva Schaefer with Stepsisters , not shown yesterday), the still-in-development punk rock Cruella 2 from Craig Gillespie starring Emma Stone, and the upcoming Beauty and the Beast -verse title, Gaston . Maleficent years ago was a great success for the studio. If that Sleeping Beauty spinoff taught Disney anything, it’s to approach live-action adaptations of the classics from the side in an edgy way rather than a full-on adaptation (i.e. Dumbo , Pinocchio , Snow White ) with great filmmakers and sublime stars. Quite often, the old pics are dated in their morals and arrive with inherent themes which are more baggage than their worth for the studio when trying to pull in a pluralistic audience. Another lesson from Moana : Don’t make a carbon copy of the original animated pic. Better to vary it up with different musical numbers and deeper plots for fun’s sake. Also when it comes to non-Disney IP movies, the current motion picture administration is on the hunt for the next YA hit, which can easily fit into the Magic Kingdom’s sensibilities both spiritually and merchandising wise, read winning a big auction for Katherine Rundell’s Impossible Creatures , a publishing phenomenon on the order of Harry Potter , The Hunger Games and Twilight Saga (no updates yesterday). Animation Is Intact With Frozen 3 , a November 2029 date for Coco 2 and Incredibles 3, clearly Disney knows when it comes to making $1 billion hits, it never fails to make a sequel to a landmark hit. And ya gotta space ’em out. Frozen 3 arrives eight years after its previous chapter, Incredibles 3 is ten years later than its predecessor while Coco 2 will hit theaters 12 years after Coco . Disney kept their powder dry on what to expect on Coco 2 and Incredibles 3 , showing very little footage. Essentially what we learned were plot reveals. Original Walt Disney Animation title, Hexed , due out at Thanksgiving, about a young woman coming into her bewitching powers while facing off against a coven, looks like it can work, elevating the leading independent female sensibility that the studio’s princess toons are known for, while also being the flip side of a Disney princess. Walton Goggins as a wisenheimer three-eyed Southern cat, Beef Roger Crummchuk, to Hailee Steinfeld’s protag, Billie Doe, is very funny and very Goggins. Disney vet Jodie Foster in her first Disney animation voiceover role as the villain, Queen Celeste, is intriguing. Well played, casting. Kristen Bell and Idina Menzel Jesse Grant/Getty Images But get ready for Frozen 3 . At the last D23 two years, they merely teased concept art, but this year, Kristen Bell and Idina Menzel (Anna and Elsa) rocked a new song, “Frozen Heart” while Josh Gad brought down the house with a new 1970s love song-sounding ditty about Olaf’s new g.f., “Samantha”. Add in a new black icy witch villain with powers that could topple Elsa and more about the ice sister’s past, and we got a great Star Wars -like film on our hands. The Jennifer Lee-directed threequel hits theaters on Nov. 24, 2027. If you want to build franchises, you have to make originals, and as we know in the current post-Covid space, sometimes that means opening at a significantly lower gross and playing out. Pixar has always won in the original space when they do their own twist on a genre (i.e. space with Wall-E , French movies with Ratatouille ) and anchor it on an emotionally affecting lead character. Not an easy needle to thread ( Elio ), but it appears they have something as they venture into horror with Ghost Market about a fast talking kid who has a supernatural interaction at a lunch shop hidden away in a remote location on Oʻahu’s North Shore that serves lost spirits, stuck between life and death. Mum’s the word on Avatar There was no mention of the future of the Na’vi last night. Two movies remain on the release calendar, Avatar 4 for Dec. 21, 2029 and Avatar 5 for Dec. 19, 2031. As far as the fate of those pics, all we know is what franchise director James Cameron has said following the threequel’s $1.48 billion (the lowest in the franchise, but, hello, still an excellent gross for any movie). They’re “still floating out there.” A New Hope for Star Wars ? Nothing new was announced, and this is the one label which requires the most resuscitation after Mandalorian and Grogu died this summer with $345M WW. Rather than getting lost in their heads on what to do with the Skywalkers or legacy characters after failing to take fans into hyperspace with 2018’s Solo: A Star Wars Story , Lucasfilm opted to go anew with elements that create alchemy, read the comedic and story awe of director Levy, scribe Jonathan Tropper and the cool and hysterically funny Gosling in Star Wars: Starfighter . It looks amazing, like Gosling’s Driver from Drive in space amid some new cool sea-filled planets. There’s an older mentor-to-kid story, and a nod to the drag race aura that George Lucas wove from his teen days into American Graffiti and Star Wars: Phantom Menace . For any die-hard Star Wars fans, there’s a lot of call-back in the imagery, but the question is whether they’ll buy into something completely fresh. The box office comp here isn’t Levy’s Deadpool & Wolverine ($211.4M domestic opening) which was working off a successful superhero comedy property, it’s more the spinoff of bigger IP, think 2016’s Fantastic Beasts coming off of Harry Potter ($74.4M domestic debut). There’s a lot of pressure on Levy and Gosling to truly take us to another galaxy far, far away next Memorial Day weekend. Meanwhile, per newly appointed co-president, Dave Filoni, when it comes to an Adam Driver starring The Hunt for Ben Solo movies; fans, it’s not the movie you’re looking for, to quote Obi-wan Kenobi. Filoni told Deadline that when it comes to the next movie after Rise of Skywalker, “The force is not with us in that regard.” This was the second time in the Disney fan confab’s history that they’ve wowed their future film and TV lineup at the Honda Centre (called D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event), taking what was once a filled theater-like presentation at the Anaheim Convention Center to what’s now an Ariana Grande-like concert spectacle with floating balloons, Broadway numbers and the entire arena doing “the wave” before the start of the show. title: Disney Leaders Talk Streaming Strategy and Growth Drivers: Sports, Local Language, Vertical Media and Emerging Formats
full_text: Aug 15, 2026 4:30pm PT Disney Leaders Talk Streaming Strategy and Growth Drivers: Sports, Local Language, Vertical Media and Emerging Formats By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Disney Leaders Talk Streaming Strategy and Growth Drivers: Sports, Local Language, Vertical Media and Emerging Formats 9 hours ago Darren Walker Opens His Home to Friends and Anonymous Content Emmy Nominees in Celebration of ‘Joy, Reflection, Delight and Awe’ 18 hours ago A Bulldog in Business: How Moving into the Booth Opened Other Doors for Dodger Great Orel Hershiser 3 days ago See All The Walt Disney Company Amid a torrent of fan-friendly news about Disney projects across the media spectrum, Disney leadership took time on the first day of the three-day D23 fan fest weekend in Anaheim for panels that offered a behind the scenes look at the Mouse House’s business strategies and vision for driving growth in the streaming era. One of the topics tackled was how to reach next-generation Disney fans with next-generation content formats to keep the company’s many franchises relevant to Gen Alpha and beyond. Disney’s push into the booming vertical media space — aka microdramas and other shortform clips designed to be viewed on mobile phones — was discussed in detail during a session with Eric Schrier , Disney’s president of Direct-to-Consumer International Originals, Strategic Programming and Emerging Media, and Erin Teague , who is executive VP of Product Management for Disney Entertainment and ESPN . Related Stories Peacock to Be Included in YouTube Premium Subscription Bundle Starting in 2027 The conversation was moderated by Jon YouShaei , a YouTube and Instagram executive turned creator and podcaster, and it also featured the perspective of Disney-centric creator Blake Silva as a panelist. Popular on Variety Schrier emphasized that the “Verts” push on Disney+ is a significant investment for the Mouse. The company last week unveiled a pact with TikTok designed to encourage more fans to create clips with authorized Disney IP. This is a big change for the company that has historically vigorously enforced its copyright and trademark rights. “We’ve always looked at making film and television in very finite formats. Half hours, hours, feature length films. And now you can tell any story. Creators are just storytellers,” Schrier said. “We’ve always talked about our creators before there were actually creators. The creator of ‘Paradise,’ Dan Fogelman, he’s a creator. We talk about them as creators. And so they’re just different types of storytellers. So how do we bring those stories to Disney+? How do we complement what we already have on platform? And it’s early days, but we’re really excited about this next generation of storytellers that are out there that are into Disney+.” Teague pointed to examples that demonstrate how smart promotion and word-of-mouth via social media helps drive viewership to Disney’s biggest investments in TV and film. Creator Blake Silva, Disney’s Eric Schrier and Erin Teague and moderator Jon Youshaei speak Aug. 14 at D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event in Anaheim. (The Walt Disney Company/Image Group L.A.) The Walt Disney Company “There will never be a replacement for that long-form original content but what is interesting is the way that it is now being supplemented by the shorter form analysis, the clips,” Teague said. As with live game coverage for sports, she said, “the additional commentary and analysis around the game is just as interesting. And so the ways that we can merge those experiences to give people exactly what they want, when they want it in a split second, I think, is the challenge.” Silva asserted that most experienced creators who hone their focus on key brands and franchises know how to plug themselves in to the company’s priorities. He said the TikTok deal and Disney+’s embrace of creator content has been invigorating for the Disney-verse. “We look at social media and clips going viral, about movies or scenes from movies all the time,” Silva said. “So imagine how that would translate and convert when they’re already in the app, to watch it immediately. I really believe in the creator to talent pipeline. It’s really exciting to think how could this create the next Mister Rogers, my idol.” Teague underscored that fans expect to be part of the action in ways that were unimaginable to their parents and grandparents. “Next generations of fans are expecting more from their entertainment experience. They want to be a part of the story. They want to put themselves in the story. They want interactivity. They want to have more agency in the storytelling experience with the democratization of creativity,” Teague said. Teague also took part in a session on how ESPN’s increasingly global sports profile is helping Disney find subscribers and fans. “ESPN is effectively synonymous with sports as a brand. So diehard sports fans know and love ESPN and have forever, that will never change. We will never stop serving the diehard, loyal sports fan because that’s our base,” Teague said during the session moderated by Joe Earley , Co-President of Direct to Consumer for Disney Entertainment. “But two trends are happening. One, the internet and native generations. Gen Alpha, Gen Z, etc. They are now expecting more from their sports fandom and their sports experience,” Teague said. “The technology is evolving and we’re thinking about how to also superserve the casual sports fan, because that fandom is equally as real. And it turns out it looks very similar to Disney fandom. And so we’re thinking about this consistently across our product experiences.” Freddy Rolón , ESPN’s head of global sports and talent office, reeled off the latest stats for ESPN’s reach with 43 linear networks in more than 130 countries and territories, and it is available on Disney+ in more than 100 markets. For the month of June, ESPN reached 640 million digital and social users. “We reach more casual fans, we reach more female fans on Disney+ and then on the flip side, ESPN brings to Disney+ a credibility about sports, authenticity about sports, and then really a recurring reason for fans to come back to the platform. Not just for the games, but for the game around the game,” Rolón said. “When we think about all those platforms, they work in concert. They’re not necessarily individual. We think about the game on Disney+, the coverage, and the social media platforms all working together to reach fans with information when they want it.” Disney’s Erin Teague, Freddy Rolón, Jo Fox and Joe Earley speak Aug. 14 at D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event in Anaheim. (The Walt Disney Company/Image Group L.A.) The Walt Disney Company Jo Fox , senior VP of marketing for ESPN, said the tighter connection to Disney+ as the platform has expanded significantly across Europe, Middle East, Asia and Latin America has been hugely beneficial. ESPN has made the strategic decision to make key programs available via Disney+ even for subscribers who don’t get the bundle. “We use the Disney+ platform and their audience, who might be different to our ESPN core audience, and we can talk to them more directly and get them more enthused about sports and ultimately engaging with Disney+ and ESPN as well,” Fox said. “So as an example of that, we will have select college football games and ‘College GameDay’ unlocked on Disney+ coming up. Because the mascots, the pageantry, the tribal nature of it, the excitement around it. It seems like an amazing sport to be able to unlock some of these select games on Disney+ and talk to this new fan base.” Earley also moderated a session on Disney+’s international content strategy for local-language production with Schrier and Carol Choi , Disney Asia Pacific’s executive VP of Integrated Marketing & APAC Original Strategy. It’s a balancing act of leveraging the platform’s worldwide reach with the need to keep subscribers engaged on a consistent basis. Local-language content has long been seen as key to reducing subscriber churn rates. “What we’re really looking to do is tell stories for local audiences and be hyper-local. We call it local for local. So we make French shows for France, Spanish shows for Spain, or Brazilian shows for Brazil. And we do that all over the world,” Schrier said. “We’re going to be increasing that significantly to have local audiences have something that expresses their culture and their sensibility. And what’s happened organically out of that local for local strategy is that those stories are now traveling back to other parts of the world.” Korea and Japan are prime areas of focus for Disney+ and local-language production. “Our local creators and storytellers really appreciate the ability for them to tell stories that are authentic to the local cultures with the support of people who’ve been telling stories like their whole career, like Eric and his team,” Choi said. “With that guidance, we’ve been very fortunate to have produced a number of hits, as well as having audiences outside of APAC discover these stories and content.” Choi pointed to recent buzzy Disney+ series including “Tempest,” “Perfect Crown” and “A Shop For Killers.” Earley added, “Some of those Korean dramas put up numbers that rival or even exceed some of the global originals as well.” (Pictured top: Disney’s Eric Schrier, Carol Choi and Joe Earley speak at D23 in Anaheim on Aug. 14.) title: Disney and Epic Games Launch Game That Connects Star Wars Theme Park Ride to New Fortnite Adventure
full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All August 15, 2026 4:30pm Millennium Falcon Smuggler's Gambit Disney/Epic Games The Walt Disney Co. and Epic Games are debuting an unprecedented new effort that will connect one of Disney’s real-life theme park rides with a bespoke adventure in Fortnite . The company’s on Saturday unveiled Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run | Fortnite , which will enable visitors to the Smuggler’s Run attraction at Disney’s theme parks in Orlando and Anaheim to accept a special mission while in the queue for the ride, and if they succeed, they will get a unique Forsworn Trooper Outfit in a newly-created Fortnite adventure called Smugglers Gambit set in that same universe. Related Stories Movies 'Frozen 3' "Royal Wedding" Between Anna and Kristoff Is Crashed by New Villain in First-Look Movies 'Zootopia 3' in the Works at Disney “ Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run | Fortnite marks the first time this attraction has reached beyond its physical walls into a connected game world — a story that starts in a queue in Orlando or Anaheim can now continue on a screen almost anywhere,” said Sean Shoptaw, executive vp of Disney Games and Digital Entertainment. “ Smugglers Gambit, built in-house by an incredibly talented team, is an immersive, high-quality game, and together these experiences reflect our ambition to connect stories and worlds across formats into one converged entertainment ecosystem.” Millennium Falcon: Smuggler’s Run is one of two flagship rides within the Galaxy’s Edge Star Wars lands at Disneyland and Walt Disney World, with visitors working together to pilot Han Salo’s famous spacecraft. The cockpit technology in the ride was actually created using Epic’s Unreal Engine, which allows for many assets from the ride to appear in Smugglers Gambit . “Building on Epic’s technology, Disney’s Imagineers are shaping the future of interactive entertainment, where an experience goes from the physical world into Fortnite,” said Adam Sussman, president of Epic Games. “Whether you’re at a Disney Park or playing Fortnite with your friends, fans have new ways to keep their Star Wars adventures going. This is only the beginning of what’s possible when world-class storytellers bring their creativity into Fortnite.” Disney, of course, is an investor in Epic Games, and the two companies have been at work building a new world that will connect to Fortnite with all of the Disney’s beloved characters. Until now, however, that collaboration has taken the form of special seasons and minigames associated with Fortnite, featuring characters from Star Wars, Marvel, The Simpsons , or other IP. This new collaboration, however, extends to the real world for the first time, bringing some video game magic to Disney’s parks, and some of that theme park magic to the video game. THR

Rosengart, shared a statement with People , which reads, “The allegations that Selena Gomez engaged in any way whatsoever in any purported ‘fraud’ or other wrongdoing are completely meritless, both factually and legally. We will vigorously defend these false allegations and indeed are filing a motion to dismiss the baseless claims against her.” Related Stories Music The Playlist: Seventeen's Vernon on His Hyperpop Roots, K-pop's Evolution and What Inspired 'V8' News Courtney Love Reveals Doctors Told Her She "Was Going to Die" in 2019: "My Body Just Exploded" Filed on Thursday, Wondermind SRS 44 LLC and Bespoke Wondermind SPV LLC sued Gomez, Teefey and Pierson for falsely representing their mental health startup’s leadership and partnerships. Wondermind, a startup focused on mental fitness practices and tools, was co-founded by the trio in November 2021, and they allegedly told investors that the brand would feature an app and be boosted by major advertising deals, celebrity photo shoots and cover stories. The suit alleges that Gomez was touted as a key part of marketing for the brand and that Pierson was pitched to investors as a “$200 million executive” with a “full slate of revenue-generating initiatives.” “The partnerships did not exist. The initiatives never materialized. The app was never built,” the complaint states. “And for three years, while the company quietly collapsed around them, not one of its founders, officers or directors said a word to the investors whose money was funding the collapse.” The complaint argues that Gomez, Teefey and Pierson allegedly committed securities fraud, common-law fraud and breach of contract; the suit seeks rescission of the investment contract and damages. title: CBS News Chief Correspondent Matt Gutman Accused of Harassment in Wrongful-Termination Suit by Former ABC News Producer
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 15, 2026 2:46pm Matt Gutman Lorenzo Bevilaqua/ABC/Getty Images CBS News correspondent Matt Gutman has been accused of workplace harassment in a wrongful-termination lawsuit filed by a former ABC News colleague, who alleges he made inappropriate comments while they worked together. Samira Said, a field producer who worked for ABC News from May 2021 until March 2025, filed the lawsuit Friday in Los Angeles Superior Court against ABC News and its parent company, The Walt Disney Co. Gutman is also named as a defendant. Said alleges that Gutman created a hostile work environment through two incidents while they were colleagues at ABC News. Related Stories TV CBS News Pushes Into Live Events as 'Sunday Morning' Teams With 92nd Street Y (Exclusive) Business David Ellison Breaks Silence on Antitrust Lawsuit: It's Not About Market Share, It's About CNN Gutman joined CBS News on Jan. 5, as chief correspondent, the first major on-air hire under CBS News editor in chief Bari Weiss. He previously served as ABC News’ chief national correspondent, where he worked in various roles for nearly two decades. According to the lawsuit, Said was placed on a “male-only team.” During one assignment, the suit alleges, “While the team waited in a public queue during the assignment, Gutman initiated a discussion rating a female correspondent’s appearance and reducing her professional standing to a numerical score based on her physical attributes. The male crew joined in, continuing to assess the woman’s body and looks in Said’s presence. The men attempted to draw Said into the conversation by soliciting her views. Said declined and stated the conversation was inappropriate.” In another alleged incident, Said and Gutman disagreed about whether the team should leave a work site while covering a press event for a movie release. “In front of multiple coworkers, Gutman responded by making a sexualized insinuation that Said must have an after-hours date in the city and that this is why she did not want to relocate,” the lawsuit states. “The remark, made audibly to others, demeaned Said and reduced her professional judgment to a sexualized stereotype.” The lawsuit’s claims against ABC and Disney extend beyond Gutman’s alleged conduct. Said alleges that the companies later mishandled her requests for medical accommodations following an assignment covering the 2022 mass shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas. According to the lawsuit, Said was assigned to interview child survivors who witnessed the killings of their classmates. Following the assignment, she “experienced severe psychological symptoms” and “was still experiencing symptoms from COVID-19,” the suit states. From August 2022 through January 2023, Said was granted medical leave, during which her “psychiatrist continued to certify the medical necessity of her leave on a recurring basis,” according to the lawsuit. By early 2023, Said’s psychiatrist had cleared her to return to work “subject to reasonable accommodations designed to enable her to perform the essential functions of the position while protecting against re-exposure to trauma triggers.” Said alleges that ABC denied her accommodation requests. She also claims that ABC News’ Los Angeles bureau chief David Herndon “made it clear that unless she returned without restrictions and with full-week availability, she would not be permitted to resume her role.” “Following her medical leave and accommodation requests, Plaintiff was subjected to materially adverse treatment than she had experienced at any time prior to engaging in protected activity,” the lawsuit states. Said alleges that she was subsequently assigned to weekend desk shifts. In January 2025, while covering the Los Angeles wildfires and other hazardous weather-related events, Said alleges that she was injured on the job when heavy equipment struck her foot, resulting in a bone contusion. According to the lawsuit, she reported the injury to her supervisors and was evaluated by a Disney physician, who determined that she did not need to take leave. ABC News terminated Said on March 5, 2025, according to the lawsuit. She is seeking compensatory and punitive damages, as well as attorneys’ fees. CBS News had no comment. The Hollywood Reporter also reached out to representatives for ABC News and Gutman but did not hear back by the time of publication. THR
